container: Economic inequality refers to the disparity in wealth and income distribution among individuals within a society. This gap can have profound effects on various aspects of life, influencing access to education, healthcare, and job opportunities. People in lower-income brackets often face obstacles in achieving upward mobility, exacerbating the cycle of poverty. High levels of inequality can lead to social unrest and decreased social cohesion, as the division between the rich and poor becomes more pronounced. Furthermore, economic inequality can hinder economic growth, as it limits the ability of a significant portion of the population to participate fully in economic activities. Addressing this issue requires comprehensive policies aimed at redistributing wealth and creating opportunities for all individuals, thereby fostering a more equitable and inclusive society.
